blocks.heading: Advertising media and online commerce
blocks.text: Media include print, radio, television, outdoor displays and online channels. Compare audience reach, cost, targeting, message detail, access and the need for sound or images. Radio can reach listeners without showing a detailed design; print or online images can show it but require suitable access and attention. Online advertising can link to an e-commerce transaction, yet a promotional webpage alone is not proof that a purchase can be completed online. E-commerce concerns buying and selling through electronic networks, with fulfilment and customer support still needed.

blocks.heading: Putting the idea to work
blocks.text: Ota Crafts wants local buyers to see the shape of a product. Some buyers access local online notices; others rely on a shop display. An image-based notice or display can show shape directly, unlike audio alone. Choose accessible media and a clear buying route; online reach does not make delivery free or automatic.

blocks.heading: E-commerce
blocks.text: E-commerce is buying and selling through electronic networks. It can let customers browse, order or pay remotely, depending on the arrangement. It can widen access but requires suitable connectivity, trust, payment arrangements and fulfilment. An online advertisement alone is promotion; a route for carrying out the purchase is the commerce function. Physical products still need collection, delivery or returns arrangements.

blocks.heading: Putting the idea to work
blocks.text: Teya Crafts accepts orders and payments online and sends the goods by a carrier. The transaction is e-commerce; the carrier is transport. The online channel does not remove physical handling cost.
